title: NI's O'Neill ruled out of Nations League matches
snippet: Arsenal forward Ceadach O'Neill is ruled out of Northern Ireland's final two Nations League fixtures against Ukraine in Belfast and Hungary in Budapest.
body: Image source, Inpho Image caption, Ceadach O'Neill came on as a substitute in wins over Georgia and Ukraine Arsenal forward Ceadach O'Neill has withdrawn from the Northern Ireland squad for the forthcoming Nations League matches against Ukraine and Hungary because of injury. O'Neill won his first senior cap against Guinea in June and came on as a late substitute in the Nations League wins over Georgia and Ukraine in the last international window. The 18-year-old, who now has four international caps, recently made his first senior appearance for Arsenal, starting in the Carabao Cup last-16 tie against Fleetwood Town, which the Gunners lost in a penalty shootout. O'Neill joins Sunderland defender Dan Ballard, Eoin Toal, and midfielders Ali McCann and Jamie McDonnell in being ruled out of the upcoming double-header because of injury. Liverpool's Conor Bradley, who has not played since January, remains a long-term absentee. Michael O'Neill's side are unbeaten at the top of League B2 with eight points from four matches and can earn promotion to the top tier for the first time. Mee and Kenny handed first Northern Ireland call-ups Published 6 days ago Kenny's background 'not that important' to O'Neill Published 6 days ago Northern Ireland face Ukraine at Windsor Park on Saturday, 14 November at 19:45 GMT, before they travel to Budapest to play Hungary in their final match on Tuesday, 17 November. Both games are live on BBC iPlayer and BBC Sounds. Manchester United goalkeeper Dermot
summary_en: Arsenal forward Ceadach O'Neill has left the Northern Ireland squad for two Nations League games because of injury.

title: Szoboszlai a doubt for Nations League conclusion
snippet: Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai will undergo tests on a knee injury to ascertain his readiness to join up with the Hungarian national side for Nations League fixtures against Georgia and Northern Ireland.
body: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Dominik Szoboszlai has made eight Premier League appearances for Liverpool this season Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai will undergo tests on a knee injury to ascertain his fitness for Hungary's Nations League fixtures against Georgia and Northern Ireland. The 26-year-old was replaced after 69 minutes of the Anfield club's 3-1 Premier League victory over Crystal Palace on Sunday. The Hungarian Football Federation have said their captain is "following the usual protocol in such cases" and that they will offer an update on his availability as soon as possible. Hungary are second in Nations League Group B2, one point behind leaders Northern Ireland who they play in the concluding fixture of the campaign in Budapest on 17 November. Before that potential decider, Marco Rossi's side travel to Georgia on Saturday. Speaking after the win over Palace that lifted the Reds up to fourth in the Premier League table, Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola said he appreciates the player will do all he can to be available for his country. "I know he will do everything to go because he loves to play with the national team, but he was not 100% when he finished the game. "I suppose they will have to analyse, the medical staff, and see what it is. "I know what I want, but I also have to understand the national teams. I'm sure that Dom, if he is fine he will want to go, but I'm not sure if he's going to be fine." Szoboszlai, along with Alexander Isak and Cod
summary_en: Liverpool's Dominik Szoboszlai faces tests on a knee problem ahead of Hungary's Nations League games.

title: Burn replaces injured Guehi in England squad
snippet: Newcastle's Dan Burn is added to the England squad to play Croatia and Spain in the Nations League this week after Marc Guehi pulls out with a hip injury.
body: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Dan Burn and Marc Guehi were both part of England's 2026 World Cup squad Senior football correspondent Published 8 November 2026 Updated 9 hours ago Newcastle's Dan Burn has been added to the England squad to play Croatia and Spain in the Nations League this week after Manchester City defender Marc Guehi pulled out with a hip injury. Guehi was substituted at half-time of City's loss at Nottingham Forest on Saturday and manager Enzo Maresca said afterwards the centre-back had requested to come off because of the injury. BBC Sport revealed on Sunday that the 26-year-old was having a scan to determine the severity of the ongoing issue, and the defender has now been ruled out of this week's matches. The former Crystal Palace captain has been a mainstay of Thomas Tuchel's team since his appointment as England head coach in January 2025. Guehi started in all but one of England's games at the World Cup and all four of the team's Nations League fixtures in September and October. Burn has 11 international caps and was also part of Tuchel's squad for the World Cup, where he made two substitute appearances. The 34-year-old has not featured for the Three Lions since after he missed the previous international break with an ankle injury. England face Croatia at Wembley on Thursday, before travelling to Madrid to face World Cup winners Spain on Saturday. summary_en: Manchester City defender Marc Guehi withdrew from the England squad with a hip injury.
